newsitem.title: GERMANY: East German spymaster calls ex-CIA chief naive.
newsitem.headline: East German spymaster calls ex-CIA chief naive.

text.p: Legendary East German spymaster Markus Wolf on Monday called a former director of the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency naive for trying to recruit him at the end of the Cold War.

Wolf, speaking at the launch of his autobiography, said ex-CIA chief William Webster tried to tempt him with a house, a small fortune and a new identity in California in exchange for the names of East German agents.
"I would describe this Webster as an inexperienced man," Wolf said. "I think this type of presentation, very friendly, polite, did not reflect a very high estimation of my intelligence."
Wolf's autobiography, "Man Without a Face" was launched in 14 countries in 11 languages on Monday and pictures the 74-year-old staring out from the cover with a steely gaze.
The elusive figure earned the title from his western counterparts, because they had little idea what he looked like during the three decades he ran East Berlin's feared foreign intelligence network.
Wolf said he had received offers from many publishing houses before deciding on U.S. giant Random House and List in Germany. He would not say how much he was paid.
Tanned and poised a week after receiving a suspended sentence from a German court for kidnapping, coercion and bodily harm during the Cold War, Wolf described his trial as purely political.
"No one in the leadership of socialist countries can say he is entirely free of guilt, but I also cannot accept moral responsibility for the entire East German system," he said.
Wolf said the kidnappings he was charged with were regrettable but they belonged to his job and were everyday occurences in Berlin during the Cold War.

He said he had been misrepresented in the German press since excerpts of the book were released last week, and denied he had implied that a former West German Social Democrat, Herbert Wehner, had been a traitor.
Wolf said Wehner had freely supplied East Germany with information about the West, but said he had not intended to hurt the late politician's reputation.
